stories.title: DRC Ebola outbreak shows no signs of slowing as deaths top 3,000
stories.summary: Congo’s Ebola outbreak has killed more than 3,000 people out of more than 6,100 confirmed cases, according to the latest government data from Wednesday, as the disease is spreading at an unprecedented speed, faster than efforts to track and slow it. Data from Congo’s Ministry of Health showed the outbreak has recorded 6,186 confirmed cases, including 3,007 deaths since it was declared a global health emergency in mid-May. It remains the fastest-growing outbreak of Ebola ever. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports.

stories.title: Iran adds more than $1bn in oil revenue to foreign reserves
stories.summary: Iran adds more than $1bn in oil revenue to foreign reserves Iran received more than $1bn in oil revenue during the 11 days to September 2, according to the semi-official Fars news agency. Fars said documents reviewed by its reporter showed that authorities had transferred the foreign currency generated by oil exports into Iran’s reserves. The inflow will strengthen the central bank’s ability to cover the country’s foreign currency requirements, the report added. Iran generated more than 80 percent of the oil income forecast in its 2026-27 budget during the first five months of the fiscal year, which began on March 21.

stories.title: EEF becomes key regional cooperation platform — Myanmar’s vice president
stories.summary: Nyo Saw highlighted that the EEF gave momentum to strengthening partnerships and seeking new ways to ensure sustainable development
article_sentences: The Eastern Economic Forum (EEF) in Russia’s Far East has become an important platform for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region, Myanmar’s Vice President Nyo Saw said.

"Amid global changes, it is this forum that gives momentum to strengthening partnerships and seeking new ways to ensure sustainable development," he pointed out in an address to the EEF plenary session.

opening: India is touting its locally manufactured AK-203 Sher assault rifle – an advanced version of Russia’s powerful Kalashnikov – as an important milestone for the “Make in India” initiative to reduce reliance on foreign-made weapon systems.
The Sher, or Tiger, will replace the older, heavily criticised Indian National Small Arms System (INSAS) service rifles used by the Indian Army.

stories.title: Senegalese consumers rally online against rising cost of living
stories.summary: In Senegal, the price of a kilogram of meat has risen from 3,800 to 5,500 CFA francs in just a few months, while the price of onions has doubled. Fuel, transportation, rent… No sector has been spared by the surge in prices. Senegalese consumers who are frustrated by the rising cost of living in Dakar have launched a new hashtag: #30DaysForTheRightPrice. The organisers of this widely shared digital campaign want to alert the authorities to the social consequences of the situation, particularly for the most vulnerable households. FRANCE 24's team on the ground reports.
